messages:
Alex G: Heads-up — seeing tail latency spikes (~300-700ms token p99) for some tenants on the eu-west multi-tenant GPU pool after the node kernel patch rolled at 03:10 UTC. Noticed around 03:12.
Priya N: Yikes. Any correlation with specific instances or AZ?
Alex G: Mostly az-b and az-c hosts. CPU steal is low, but NVLink utilization is through the roof on those hosts.
Mateo R: Can you drop the pprof trace or nvidia-smi output?
Alex G: Paste logs below from one affected host:
```
03:11:42 gpu0  util 98%  mem 73%  nvlink 92%
03:11:43 gpu1  util 97%  mem 70%  nvlink 89%
03:11:44 net  egress 1.2Gb/s  interrupts spiking
kernel: rcu_sched detected stall on CPU 5
```
Jing: kernel patch was the recent rcu/backport that tightened rcu stall detection. Could be surfacing previously-hidden stalls.
Priya N: Could also be our allocator switching to a different PCIe scheduler after the patch. Any change in CUDA/NVML errors?
Alex G: No CUDA errors, just elevated NVLink and longer model-kv fetch times. Prefix cache hit rate dropped ~20% for the affected tenants.
Sam (oncall-bot): Incident created: INC-2026-042 (multi-tenant eu-west tail-latency). Pager notified: oncall.
Mateo R: I'm temp-suspending kernel rollout in eu-west and reverting one host to previous kernel, will report back.
Alex G: Thanks. Also seeing increased inter-GPU memcpy times in traces (x2). That points at intra-node bus contention.
Priya N: While Mateo reverts, can we route latency-sensitive customers to dedicated pools in eu-west-2 as a temporary mitigation? That should lower customer impact.
Jing: Can we apply a soft-affinity rule to prefer single-GPU placements for short-seq requests? Reduces cross-GPU traffic.
Mateo R: Revert done on host i-0a3b7c. Preliminary metrics: NVLink util dropped to 42%, p99 token latency back near baseline (~120ms).
Alex G: Nice. Can you share the exact host id? I'll pull the qlog and check tenant allocations.
Mateo R: i-0a3b7c, rolled back at 03:21 UTC. I'll keep it in old kernel pool and quarantine until root cause fully understood.
Priya N: I'm opening a routing change to divert high-QPS small-seq traffic to dedicated pools eu-west-2 and fallback to eu-west-1. Will throttle auto-scaler to avoid migrations.
Sam (oncall-bot): Routing change PR: https://git.internal/repo/changes/PR-4766 (link posted)
Alex G: Quick diagnostic commands I'm running:
```
kubectl -n gpu get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=i-0a3b7c
nvidia-smi topo --matrix
perf record -a -g sleep 10
```
Jing: Longer-term we should add NVLink contention metrics to pool health (nvlink_util_per_gpu) and a scheduler predicate to avoid co-locating high-throughput tenants on same node.
Mateo R: Agreed. Also thinking about a cheap heuristic: detect sustained nvlink >80% and proactively pin new small-seq requests to other nodes for 5min.
Priya N: Cost note: moving traffic to dedicated pools will increase token cost ~12% for the diverted tenants. Ping product/CS for heads-up.
Alex G: I'll draft a short RCA template for CS: summary, affected tenants, mitigation, follow-ups.
Sam (oncall-bot): INC-2026-042 updated: mitigations applied, monitoring in watch. Assigned: Mateo R, Jing.
Mateo R: Next steps: (1) run microbench across kernel versions to confirm interaction with NVLink stack, (2) add nvlink metrics to pool health, (3) implement soft-affinity predicate. I'll own 1 and 3.
Jing: I'll prototype the metric ingestion and alert thresholds.
Priya N: I'll notify product and schedule a customer comms sync.
Alex G: Thanks everyone. Will keep thread updated if other nodes show regressions.
Mateo R: Follow-up: added quick probe that pings nvlink counters every 30s for all eu-west nodes. No new regressions in last 20m.
Alex G: Closing the immediate incident if no more spikes in 30m. Leaving follow-ups active.
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 status -> monitoring; next update in 30m.
